output.headline: Aledade's $271M same-sub-sector Health IT deal in 2020 and national partner network make it a credible, high-paying strategic for this target.
output.differentiator: Pays a 23.9x median, above every other buyer on the priority list bar one strategic; unlike Evolent Health and Privia Health, its precedent is a National deal [T:record].
output.why_them: Same-sub-sector buyer with a national footprint; paid up before

acquirer_overview.title: Physician-led value-based care partner with a single prior deal
points: Private; became a Public Benefit Corporation in 2023. It describes itself as physician-led and partners with clinicians rather than owning practices [P:1, P:2].
Partners are located in 46 states and the District of Columbia; its ACOs generated more than $1B in shared savings in 2024 [P:3, P:4].
Record: 1 deal, 1 of 1 closed (100%), in 2020 [T:record, K:closed_share].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Same-sub-sector focus is the strongest factor in its likelihood
points: Share of deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor; regional and margin fit are modest factors in its favour [S:sector_share, S:geo_fit, S:margin_fit].
Its 2020 deal was tagged Technology Capability (1 of 1 deals, against 10% of all deals in the file) and Vertical Integration [M:technology_capability, M:vertical_integration].
Having bought from this kind of seller is a slight factor against. It sits 4th on the priority list, likelihood 3.8% [S:own_fit_s, R:rank].

precedent_activity.title: One precedent, in the target's own sub-sector and size band
points: Oak Health Informatics: $271M, 2020, Minority Investment, 23.9x EV/EBITDA, 5.73x EV/Revenue, closed [D:MA-2020-0093].
That deal sits in the comparable size band ($150M-$600M) and in the National region [K:size_band, K:by_region].
No deals since 2022, and no control deals: 0 of 1 (0%) [K:recent, K:control_share].

valuation_context.title: Anchor at the median; this buyer has paid above the upper quartile
points: 13 comparable deals, all in the same sub-sector: 19.4x at the lower quartile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the upper quartile [V:comps].
Target margin of 25.0% is above the comps' median of 22.2% but not in their top quarter, so the 50th percentile is the defensible anchor [V:comps].
Its own median paid is 23.9x, above the comps' upper quartile. Synergy headroom is $14M-$23M; buyer revenue not researched [V:comps, V:synergy].

risk_flags.title: Thin acquisition record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal on file, with none since 2022, so repeat appetite is unproven.
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal was in the target's own sub-sector and size band, and it closed.
risk_flags.reality: A single 2020 precedent; no deals since 2022 [T:record, K:recent, K:size_band].

risk_flags.title: Minority and partnership model
risk_flags.concern: A full control purchase of a PE-backed company would depart from how it has invested.
risk_flags.mitigant: Its 2020 deal was $271M, similar in size to this target's $300M.
risk_flags.reality: 0 of 1 deals were control deals; it describes itself as a partner, not an owner of practices [K:control_share, P:2].

risk_flags.title: Price and capacity
risk_flags.concern: Its 23.9x median paid is above the comps' upper-quartile 23.3x.
risk_flags.mitigant: Synergy headroom of $14M-$23M supports a bid above the median.
risk_flags.reality: The defensible anchor is the median; its balance-sheet capacity is not researched [V:comps, V:synergy].

conviction.rationale: Only 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector keeps the sub-sector basis neutral; that deal in the target's region is the one point in its favour [C:conviction, T:record].
